title: Supplier onboarding, purchase routing, and billing-to-revrec linkage — Operational Guide
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This operational guide documents the end-to-end process for supplier onboarding, purchase order (PO) routing, invoice intake and routing, and how procurement events map to revenue recognition and billing systems. It is intended for finance operations, procurement coordinators, legal reviewers, and product owners who approve spend. The document ties procurement controls to budget/forecast gates and describes automation patterns used in NetSuite (NS), our AP workflow, and billing mappings in Redwood Billing.

Goals
- Reduce PO-to-payment cycle time to < 30 days for standard vendors.
- Ensure 100% of external contracts are captured in Contract Repository before first payment.
- Enforce delegated approval limits to maintain segregation of duties.
- Maintain a reproducible mapping from procurement line items to revenue/billing codes for proper RevRec treatment.

Scope
- New supplier onboarding (domestic and international).
- One-time purchases and recurring vendor contracts.
- Invoice submission, three-way match exceptions, and AP routing.
- How procurement events are tagged for billing and revenue recognition.
- Excludes payroll, employee reimbursements (see People Ops spend playbook).

Key Roles and Owners
- Finance Ops (Maya Chen) — overall owner of PO & AP workflows, GL mapping, RevRec mappings.
- Procurement Coordinator — supplier verification, vendor creation.
- Legal — contract review and signature.
- Product / Budget Owner — budget approval and cost-center assignments.
- Accounts Payable (AP) — invoice validation and payment execution.
- IT — SSO and vendor portal integrations.

High-level Process Flow
1. Request & Budget Validation
   1.1. Requester submits procurement request via Redwood Procurement Portal (Concur integrated form).
   1.2. Portal performs automated budget check against active forecasts and available committed budget. Failure routes to Product/Budget Owner for manual approval.
2. Supplier Onboarding
   2.1. Procurement Coordinator runs vendor screening (Sanctions/PEP) using SalsaWatch CLI: `salsawatch search --email vendor@example.com --country CN`.
   2.2. Collect W-9/W-8, banking details, and insurance certificates. Store docs in Vendor Vault (encrypted S3).
   2.3. Legal verifies contract template and marks as "Ready for Signature" in Contract Repository.
   2.4. Vendor record created in NetSuite with a unique vendor code: VND-YYYY-####.
3. PO Issuance & Routing
   3.1. For purchases > $25k, procurement must create a PO; for recurring SaaS or cloud spend, create master PO with SOW reference.
   3.2. Approval routing according to delegated limits (see Approval Matrix).
   3.3. PO sent to vendor with required billing and ship-to instructions.
4. Invoice Intake & Match
   4.1. Vendor submits invoice to ap-invoices@redwood.ai or via Vendor Portal.
   4.2. AP performs automated three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice).
   4.3. If match fails, create an exception ticket in Zendesk for Procurement Coordinator to resolve.
5. Payment & RevRec Tagging
   5.1. On payment approval, AP posts invoice to NetSuite and triggers GL entries.
   5.2. Procurement Ops must ensure each invoice line has a billing mapping tag (BillingCode) that links the procurement spend to a product revenue SKU for RevRec.

Approval Matrix (summary)
| Approval Level | Max Single Transaction | Approver Role | Secondary Approver Required |
|---------------|------------------------:|---------------|----------------------------:|
| Tier 1 | $0 - $5,000 | Team Lead | No |
| Tier 2 | $5,001 - $25,000 | Manager | No (unless cross-team) |
| Tier 3 | $25,001 - $100,000 | Director | Yes (Finance Ops) |
| Tier 4 | $100,001+ | VP or CFO | Yes (Legal + Finance Ops) |

Controls and Compliance Checklist
- Contract signed and uploaded before first payment (signature recorded in Contract Repository).
- Vendor AML/Sanctions check completed and documented.
- Insurance & SOC2 evidence for vendors handling customer data.
- Bank account verified via micro-deposit or Plaid for ACH vendors.
- Tax forms (W-9/W-8BEN) on file.

Invoice Routing and Exception Handling (detailed)
- Standard Invoice Flow: Vendor -> ap-invoices@redwood.ai -> AP auto-parse -> NetSuite PO match -> Payment scheduled.
- Exceptions:
  - Missing PO: If invoice has no linked PO, route to Procurement Coordinator. If spending under $1,000 and internal card used, follow corporate card reconciliation instead.
  - Amount Variance (>5%): Flagged, routed to Budget Owner for approval; if unresolved within 5 business days, hold payment and escalate to Director.
  - Rate/Deliverable Dispute: Mark invoice status "Disputed" and notify vendor with dispute ticket template.

Vendor Onboarding: Minimum Documents (table)
- Vendor master creation checklist:
  - Company legal name (string)
  - Tax ID / EIN (string)
  - W-9 or W-8 type (file)
  - Banking routing + account (encrypted)
  - Point of contact + email
  - SOC2/ISO attestation (if handling customer data)
  - Insurance certificate (limits >= $1M per occurrence)

Billing Code & RevRec Linkage (operational guidance)
- Each procurement line must include a BillingCode in PO line metadata. BillingCode values are managed by Finance Ops and map 1:1 (or 1:many) to Revenue SKU(s).
- Examples:
  - BillingCode: infra-gpu-hours -> maps to Revenue SKU: compute-addon-1 -> RevRec treatment: immediate recognition on invoice if matched to pass-through cost, or amortize over term if vendor is for customer-facing feature (see RevRec rules below).
  - BillingCode: thirdparty-ml-license -> maps to Revenue SKU: model-licensing -> RevRec: amortize over contract term using ASC 606 pattern.

RevRec Rules Summary (finance policy excerpt)
- Pass-through reimbursable costs: Recognize when customer invoiced (matching principle).
- Vendor services that enable customer functionality (SaaS add-ons): Recognize ratably over the service term.
- Capitalizable procurement (hardware): Capitalized and depreciated per CapEx policy; depreciation expense recognized in SG&A; only recognized in revenue if resold.

Automation & Integrations
- NetSuite connectors: PO creation and invoice posting automated via Redwood Finance API (internal) — endpoints: POST /finance/v1/po, POST /finance/v1/invoice.
- Vendor Portal: SSO via Okta; documents stored in Vendor Vault buckets with lifecycle policy 7 years for tax/legal.
- Billing mapping sync: nightly job `billing-sync` that pulls PO/invoice metadata and updates BillingCode -> Revenue SKU crosswalk in RevRec service.

Operational SLAs and Metrics
- PO issuance SLA: 90% of approved requests receive PO within 3 business days.
- PO to first payment: target median 18 days.
- Exception resolution: 95% within 7 business days.
- Contract capture: 100% of signed contracts in repository before payment.

Change Orders and Amendments
- Any scope change that modifies price or term by >10% requires an amendment executed in Contract Repository and a new PO or PO amendment in NetSuite referencing the amendment ID.
- Amendment workflow: Product Owner -> Finance Ops assessment -> Legal amendment -> Signatures (e-sign enabled).

Sample Communication Templates
- Vendor Invoice Missing PO (email):
  Subject: Redwood - Invoice {invoice_no} requires PO
  Body: Hello {vendor_contact}, we received invoice {invoice_no} but could not find a matching PO. Please confirm the PO number or submit an updated invoice referencing PO {po_number}. Open ticket: {zendesk_link}.

- Dispute Notice (to vendor):
  Subject: Invoice {invoice_no} - Disputed Line Items
  Body: Hi {vendor_contact}, line items 2-4 on invoice {invoice_no} are under dispute due to pricing variance. We will hold payment for those lines pending resolution. Contact: procurement@redwood.ai.

Training and Onboarding for Stakeholders
- Procurement Coordinator checklist training (1 hr): vendor screen, NetSuite vendor creation, Contract Repository tagging.
- Budget Owner onboarding (30 min): using Procurement Portal, approving exceptions, interpreting BillingCodes.
- AP training (2 hrs): NetSuite match rules, exception handling, payment runs.

Audit & Reporting Requirements
- Quarterly internal audit of 10% of payments for contract capture and three-way match integrity.
- Year-end tax report: vendors with >$600 aggregated payments must have appropriate tax forms; Finance Ops generates 1099s via NetSuite.

Appendices
A. Common BillingCode list (subset):
- infra-gpu-hours
- infra-network-egress
- thirdparty-ml-license
- consulting-engagement-hourly
- data-labeling-per-unit

B. Quick CLI examples
- Create vendor in NetSuite (sandbox):
  `redwood-fin create-vendor --name "Acme ML Labs" --tax-id 12-3456789 --bank-acc encrypted://vault/acc-123`
- Run sanctions check: `salsawatch search --duns 123456789`

C. Escalation contacts

- Finance Ops: finance-ops@redwood.ai (Maya Chen)
